scientific_confound: Source time-matched available habitat and observed habitat switching may both depend on day-versus-night movement behavior; the previous birdyear×prior-state×season fixed effects did not separately control photoperiod.
question: Within candidate tagged bird, prior habitat class, source winter season and source day/night label, does lower availability of the previously occupied habitat predict actual categorical switches?
source_cohort: Exact same source-verified USGS DOI 10.5066/P9ELSUHN seven-category dataset, 329 parent eligible bird-years and 56,591 original consecutive 55–65-minute event pairs. No changing species, year or source file.
eligibility: Retain only adjacent steps with matching source-recorded seasons AND matching observed photoperiod (day or night). Report both number lost for season changes and additional number lost for photoperiod boundary crossings. Do not infer sunrise/sunset from local clock.
predictor: Same exact x = 1 - current source available destination fraction in the immediately prior used habitat class.
response: Same exact y = 1 if current observed destination habitat category differs from prior observed category.
fixed_effect: Within each birdyear × immediately prior habitat class × source season × source photoperiod label, demean x/y; candidate tag pool across bird-years; minimum 20 informative pair observations per tag.
bootstrap: 10,000 source candidate stable-ID bootstrap replicates of equal-tag mean slopes. Report all four species, including non-support.
shifts: Quarter/half season rotations of complete 7-category availability vector within each source birdyear × source season × photoperiod group, not across day/night. Keep same original y/prior category and matched transition set. Four shifts fixed to ±quarter and ±half. Descriptive only.
support: Positive mean beta and candidate-tag bootstrap 95% interval lower bound >0 in >=2 of 4 species supports a broad opportunity-switch association conditional on photoperiod. To claim time alignment beyond day/night, require the observed slope to exceed all four day/night-preserving shifted slopes in >=2 species; report all outcomes even if adverse.
interpretation_limits: Post-result sensitivity not untouched confirmation; any weaker or reversed effects must downgrade the main opportunity-switch interpretation.
Day/night stratification reduces diurnal confounding but does not remove spatial autocorrelation, origin-dependent availability, movement constraints or habitat patch fidelity.
Photoperiod shifts are still descriptive non-exchangeable negative controls, not randomization p values.
Do not use results to claim adaptive tracking, energetic state regulation or conservation intervention effect.
